Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

range noun

a variety of things of one kind

also a range of, a wide range of, a variety of, selection, assortment

classical

Cic. Fin. 2.10
Phaedr. 4 epil. 2: cōpiōsa abundat rērum varietās
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 14: varietāte frūctuum (Lewis & Short)

varietās, varietātis f.

noun, third declension

variety, a range of different things

Properly of mixed colours, then of anything made up of unlike things (Cicero, Fin. 2.10).

Other words

  • omnis generis — of every kind: a whole range of

    also used · classical · Liv. 10.21.3: dīlēctum omnis generis hominum habērī jussit; Liv. 21.12.8: concursus omnis generis hominum

    The genitive of genus, kind (see kind).

Examples

  • adhūc supersunt multa quae possim loquī, et cōpiōsa abundat rērum varietās

    there is still much left that I could tell, and a rich range of materialPhaedr. 4 epil. 1–2

  • varietās enim Latīnum verbum est, idque propriē quidem in disparibus colōribus dīcitur, sed trānsfertur in multa disparia: varium poēma, varia ōrātiō, variī mōrēs, varia fortūna

    for variety is a Latin word, and properly it is said of different colours, but it is carried over to many things that differ: a varied poem, varied speech, varied ways, varied fortuneCic. Fin. 2.10

See also kind, different, mountain range, range.
